messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime-latency-detector: sudden p95/p99 uplift observed for streaming ingest endpoints in us-east-1 beginning 4980012340. p95 ~1.6s -> 2.9s, p99 ~2.8s -> 6.1s. Auto-page oncall.

oncall: on duty, joining channel. what's affected? route names?

leah: quick glance at the dashboard: ingest.stream.append, ingest.stream.start, webhooks.stream.deliver. link: https://dash.redwood.company/d/latency/streams?env=prod&region=us-east-1

tom: I see a spike in request queue length on worker-group-7 (fifo depth ~ 1200). Pod counts are steady. CPU/GPU are under normal load, but disk wait (iowait) on nodes spikes concurrently.

jia: grabbed node stats: /var/log/sysstat shows high softirq and io wait, iostat shows high await on nvme1n1. Could be slow underlying storage affecting KV and local checkpoints.

raj: KV-store metrics: request latency distribution tailing, and a burn of read retries to external metadata store (NFS) via kv-proxy. kv_proxy_retries per second jumped 8x.

oncall: support-bot: No inbound Support tickets yet, but CS monitoring flagged elevated error traces for a couple of high-volume customers.

leah: immediate mitigations proposal:
- route 15% of new streaming traffic to region fallback us-east-2
- enable stateless-fallback for streaming ingest for new sessions (bypass KV checkpoint on start)
- cordon and reprovision 2 nodes in worker-group-7 with fresh NVMe (fast reprovision) if disk driver looks flaky

tom: can we test region fallback quickly? command:
```
redwood route split set --route ingest.stream.start --region us-east-1 --fallback-region us-east-2 --percent 15
```

jia: adding temp alert: disk await > 50ms on any worker-group-7 node for 5m. Also add KV proxy retry rate > 5/s for 3m.

oncall: applying route split now. will report back in 60s.

(oncall +00:01) oncall: split applied. monitoring metrics.

leah: enabling stateless-fallback feature flag for streaming start only: ff set streaming_stateless_start=true --scope=prod --region=us-east-1 --percent=20

raj: FYI root traces show repeated NFS op retries: `NFS: server 10.10.20.5 delayed response` and grpc to kv-store returns deadlines for checkpoint fetch. That maps to the disk IO spike.

tom: can infra confirm NFS mgmt plane? pinging infra on-call.

(oncall +00:03) oncall: quick metric snapshot: overall p99 for streaming endpoints dropped from 6.1s -> 2.4s after fallback + stateless-fallback. Queue depth down ~35%.

support-bot: CS: Assigned AE for potentially impacted accounts (sent initial heads-up).

leah: good progress. next steps for live mitigation: 1) increase fallback to 40% if stable for 10m, 2) reprovision two workers with fresh NVMe and run fio to validate IO, 3) infra to look into NFS server latency and consider failover, 4) open incident ticket for postmortem.

raj: capturing logs and correlating client session IDs that hit high tail. Looks like long-lived webhooks (10+ minute sessions) had higher chance of hitting tail.

tom: quick workaround: reduce default in-flight window for streaming sessions from 16 -> 8 for us-east-1 to limit queue buildup. config flag:
```
redwood config set streaming.inflight_window 8 --env=prod --region=us-east-1
```

oncall: applied inflight_window change. will observe.

(oncall +00:07) oncall: after both inflight reduction and stateless fallback increased to 35%, p95 back to ~1.4s and p99 ~2.1s. tail events still sporadic on specific customers.

leah: assign follow-ups: infra (raj) to run NFS failover and health check, infra to reprovision nodes, platform (tom) to review fio results and NVMe driver versions, product to notify major customers via AE.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: Severity P2. Live mitigations applied: region fallback, stateless-fallback, inflight window reduction. Start 4980012340, mitigation applied 4980012395. Please link postmortem when available.

oncall: documenting commands executed and metric snapshots. handing off to infra for deeper RCA. closing live triage at 4980012467. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
